newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P assigns AAA rating to Norway's Statnett SF.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns AAA rating to Norway's Statnett SF.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard and Poor's (S&P) on Tuesday said it had assigned an AAA rating to Norway's state-owned electricity group Statnett SF with a stable outlook.

The agency also assigned an A-1+ short-term isseur credit rating to Statnett, which is responsible for the operation, maintenance and development of the national electricity grid in Norway and its connections with other Nordic and European countries.

"Statnett's ratings are based on very strong implicit sovereign support for its obligations, reflecting the 100 percent state-owned utility's legal status as a state enterprise, and its economic importance as the national grid company," S&P said in a statement.
"The legal structure assures the ultimate guarantee of the Kingdom of Norway, which has a AAA foreign currency rating with a stable outlook, on all Statnett's obligations."
Statnett was formed in 1992 following the division of the Statskraftverkene, the state power board, and the 1991 deregulation of the Norwegian electric industry.
S&P said the stable outlook reflected the state ownership of the group.
Statnett has a monopoly transmission operation in Norway which is key to the country's economy, S&P said.

"The stable outlook reflects the vital role of Statnett in the Norwegian economy and the strong support provided by the owner, the Kingdom of Norway, through Statnett's state enterprise status," S&P said.
